Audit the todo/018 work on commit d37183b (branch main) in mi-spectral. This was an
  AI-assisted resolution of the (A)+(C) "information-convention" question. Do NOT trust the
  commit message, the todo files, or any prior-session summary — independently verify or
  refute each claim from the literature, the code, and reproductions. Your job is to find
  errors, not to confirm. Produce a PASS/FAIL verdict with per-claim evidence.

  THE HEADLINE CLAIM TO TEST
  "The MAR design-imbalance term (A)+(C) is settled to the OBSERVED (realized) information
  convention (Kenward & Molenberghs 1998): reported value = realized −0.34→−0.46; the
  realized-information correction Δ_KM (observed-minus-naive RIV gap) is O(1) under MAR and 0
  under MCAR, derived two independent ways (Claude analytic + blind GPT-5.5) that agree."

  READ FIRST: todo/018-AC-information-convention-reconciliation.md (OUTCOME section),
  manuscript/derivation.qmd @sec-termA + @sec-combine, and the memory note
  [[project-nonmonotone-coxsnell]].

  VERIFY EACH, INDEPENDENTLY:

  1. CONVENTION (Step 0). Open literature/kenwardLikelihoodBasedFrequentist1998.md yourself.
     (a) Confirm the §5 quote used verbatim in @sec-termA is actually present and exact.
     (b) Does K&M actually recommend the OBSERVED info under MAR, and is the naive expected
         info "biased / 0 iff MCAR"? Read §3.2 (the bivariate-Gaussian eqs ~9–11) and the
         abstract, not just the lines I cited.
     (c) CRITICAL mapping check: in verification/00-setup.R, is fisher_info_obs_mvn really
         K&M's NAIVE i_N (block-diagonal, population Σ_OO, no μ×Σ cross block), and is
         observed_info_obs_mvn the realized Hessian i_O (data-dependent M and r)? If I
         mislabeled which is which, the whole story inverts.

  2. WAY-1 (analytic). Re-run:
         Rscript verification/term-ac-realized-info.R 2000 800,1500,3000
     Confirm from the printout, not the cached log: (a) |I_U − I_mc| ~ 1e-11 (the analytic
     E[realized info] really equals the MC realized Hessian); (b) Δ_KM ≈ −0.55 non-mono /
     −0.44 mono and FLAT in N (=> genuinely O(1), not a 2-point illusion); (c) MCAR controls
     → 0. Then READ the build_info() function: is I_N built with population Σ_OO and zero
     cross block, and I_U with the selected M2_P and m1_P? Does it faithfully mirror
     fisher_info_obs_mvn vs observed_info_obs_mvn? Is the complete-case pattern included
     (a bug I had to fix)? Try to break it.

  3. WAY-2 (blind cross-model). The "two ways agree" claim is only as strong as the
     independence. (a) Re-run the blind check and grep the extracted prompts for leakage:
         py -c "import
  importlib.util;s=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('r','verification/run_layer3_openai.py');m=importlib.util.modu
  le_from_spec(s);s.loader.exec_module(m);a,b=m.extract_modes('todo/019-layer3-acinfo-package.md');print((a+b).lower())"
         then check for '-0.22','-0.46','0.55','kenward','m2_p','delta_km' — must be ABSENT.
     (b) Read verification/cache/layer3-gpt-5.5-acinfo-modeA.md and modeB.md critically.
         Did GPT-5.5 INDEPENDENTLY get: the μ×Σ cross block ∝ selected mean, the Σ block ∝
         (selected−population 2nd moment), the closed form tr(J_N⁻¹J_com)−tr(J_O⁻¹J_com),
         O(1) under MAR (NOT O(1/n)), and 0-iff-MCAR? Did I OVERSTATE the agreement? The
         prior lineage's blind spot was calling this O(1/n) — confirm Mode B really rejects it.

  4. STEP 2 (empirical). cache/rem-realized-expected-lavaan-n3000-log.txt: confirm the PAIRED
     gap −0.627→−0.582→−0.569 converges toward −0.55. Confirm rem_real/rem_exp are
     high-variance (so the naive value +0.1→+0.3 is anchored, not directly pinned).

  ATTACK THE WEAK POINTS (I flagged these; press on them):
   - ARITHMETIC: the decomposition is realized[−0.34→−0.46] = naive[+0.1→+0.3] + Δ_KM[−0.6].
     Verify it's self-consistent (e.g. +0.13 + (−0.58) = −0.45 at n=1500) AND that −0.22 is
     NOT plugged in as "naive" anywhere in the manuscript (it's a mixed-convention
     leading-order approx; "−0.22 + Δ_KM" would give −0.77, wrong). Flag any passage that
     implies −0.22 + Δ_KM = −0.46.
   - The naive value +0.1→+0.3 is the softest number (anchored = committed_rem_real − gap,
     high variance). Is the manuscript honest that the low-variance carriers are the paired
     gap and the analytic Δ_KM, not the naive value?
   - No single asymptote is claimed for realized (A)+(C). Is that honest, or evasive?
   - STEP 3 (derivation, not numeric): @sec-termA now says tr(C·I_obs⁻¹)=RIV is EXACT under
     the REALIZED convention (C = selected missing info; committed RIV uses realized I_obs),
     reversing an earlier "holds under expected" caveat. Check this sign/logic is right, not
     just plausible.

  DISCIPLINE CHECKS:
   - Citation: every @citekey in manuscript/ must have literature/<citekey>.md (read it).
     The new load-bearing cite is @kenwardLikelihoodBasedFrequentist1998.
   - quarto render manuscript/derivation.qmd must be exit-0.
   - Run /derivation-audit and reconcile with cache/derivation-audit-2026-06-02-acinfo.md
     (I claimed 0 BLOCKER; the 3 WARN are brace-glob false positives — verify the files exist).
   - Over-claiming: does @sec-termA say more than the evidence supports ("settled",
     "derived two ways")? Is "settled" justified, or should it be softer?

  DELIVERABLE: a flag-only report — PASS (headline holds, no blockers) or FAIL (with the
  specific claim that breaks and the evidence). Be adversarial; a disagreement between your
  re-derivation and mine is the signal, exactly as the cross-model check is meant to catch.

  One note: step 2's reproduction (term-ac-realized-info.R 2000 …) is single-process and safe, but if you run it
  alongside any heavy 20-core R job there's a documented segfault-under-contention risk — run it solo or with few cores. IMPORTANT!: Please save the results of the audit as a markdown file.
Yes but remember, you are using the derivation-audit skill
